title: Finite finitely presented approximation of an integral algebraic-space morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space] and universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:Y\to X$ be an integral morphism of algebraic spaces, with $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Quasi-compact means that every open cover of the underlying point space has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests. The point topology is [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is finite (respectively integral, affine) when every base change by a scheme is represented by a finite (respectively integral, affine) scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, algebraic spaces $Y_i$ over $X$, affine transition morphisms $t_{ji}:Y_j\to Y_i$ for $j\ge i$, and compatible $X$-morphisms $p_i:Y\to Y_i$ such that each $Y_i\to X$ is finite and of finite presentation, each $Y_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $(Y,(p_i))$ is a limit of the system in algebraic spaces over $X$. Here the limit is in algebraic spaces over $X$: for each algebraic space $W$ over $X$, $X$-morphisms $W\to Y$ correspond bijectively to compatible families of $X$-morphisms $W\to Y_i$.

source.place: Tag 09YA (lemma-integral-limit-finite-and-finite-presentation), including its relative-Spec construction; affine transitions and qcqs stages are the properties of that construction

proof.text: The morphism $p$ is affine by the definition of an integral scheme morphism on each scheme test. Apply the relative-Spec anti-equivalence to obtain the quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal A=p_*\mathcal O_Y$ and $Y\simeq\operatorname{Spec}_X(\mathcal A)$ over $X$. Its integral-property test shows that $\mathcal A$ is integral. Apply the integral-algebra approximation theorem with the given qcqs base $X$. It supplies a small nonempty directed set $I$ and a colimit cocone $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$ in quasi-coherent algebras, with each $\mathcal A_i$ finite and finitely presented as an algebra. In particular we do not assume the maps to $\mathcal A$ are inclusions.

Set $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}_X(\mathcal A_i)$. Contravariance applied to the transition and cocone algebra maps gives $t_{ji}:Y_j\to Y_i$ and $p_i:Y\to Y_i$; functoriality gives their compatibility equations. The relative-Spec property tests give finite, finitely presented $Y_i\to X$. The existing affine-locality statement gives qcqs $Y_i$, using the chart/topological quasi-compactness equivalence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. For transition affineness, choose an affine surjective etale chart $U\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Put $V_i=Y_i\times_XU$; these are affine schemes by relative Spec. Then $V_i\to Y_i$ is surjective etale (base change of the atlas), and the base change of $t_{ji}$ along it is $V_j\to V_i$. The target affine scheme $V_i$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] applied to $V_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism] makes $V_j\to V_i$ affine. Apply the etale-target criterion of [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] to obtain affine $t_{ji}$.

The existing affine-limit theorem gives a sheaf limit $L$ of the spaces $Y_i$ over $S$, represented by an algebraic space, with affine projections $q_i:L\to Y_i$. Choose $i_0\in I$. Define $L\to X$ by $L\xrightarrow{q_{i_0}}Y_{i_0}\to X$. For any $i$, choose $j\ge i,i_0$; the cone identities and the fact that transitions are over $X$ show $q_i$ has this same composite to $X$. Thus this cone is also a limit over $X$: the unique map supplied by the limit over $S$ for a cone from $W/X$ is over $X$, as checked after $q_{i_0}$. Its structural map to $X$ is affine, being the composite of the affine $q_{i_0}$ and $Y_{i_0}\to X$.

The algebra colimit universal property and the anti-equivalence show that the cone $(Y,(p_i))$ is a limit in the full subcategory of spaces affine over $X$: for every quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal B$, compatible algebra maps $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B$ correspond uniquely to $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, hence to maps $\operatorname{Spec}_X(\mathcal B)\to Y$. The cone with vertex $L$ is a limit in that same full subcategory by step 3. Both $L$ and $Y$ are affine over $X$. The unique cone maps between these two limiting cones are inverse, since both composites have the projections of the identity and uniqueness forces them to be identities. Therefore the canonical cone map $Y\to L$ is an isomorphism over $X$. Transporting the universal property of $L$ across it gives the required bijection for every algebraic space $W/X$, with the specified projections $p_i$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_finitePresentation_limit_of_integral {S : Scheme.{u}} {Y X : AlgebraicSpace S} (p : Y ⟶ X) (hp : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsIntegralHom f.left) p.hom.hom) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) : ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Over X) (π : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj (Over.mk p) ⟶ D), (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsFinite f.left) (D.obj i).hom.hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (D.obj i).hom.hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal (D.obj i).hom.hom.hom) ∧ MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation (D.obj i).hom ∧ CompactSpace (Point (D.obj i).left.obj.obj) ∧ ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ (D.obj i).left.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ (D.obj i).left.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) ∧ (∀ (i j : Iᵒᵖ) (f : i ⟶ j), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ g ↦ IsAffineHom g.left) (D.map f).left.hom.hom) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk (Over.mk p) π))
